C-01.rationale: Largest single Contraction driver and still the best-evidenced one: European private label at about half of units and 42% of value, growing again in 2026. Kept as the anchor of the private-label mechanism; the premium own-label tier point from X-10 and X-13 is folded in.
C-01.corrections: 45% German laundry PL and 30% hair PL claims were wrong (laundry about 20% value, cleaners about 30%, hair low); brand geography fixed (Lacura/Cien compete with Schauma, Persil, Perwoll, Pril); GP1 0.25 to 0.22.
C-01.base_name: Private Label Structural Penetration in Europe

C-02.rationale: Real, North America-led demand reshaping; the hair-shedding side effect is now documented in dermatology cohorts. Kept with a smaller weight because HCB's categories see only a slice of the effect.
C-02.corrections: Adoption figures updated (11-12% of US adults); JP Morgan USD 116bn replaced by USD 200bn incretin market; unsupported laundry-frequency and 12-18-month-lag sentences deleted; probability 5 to 4, GP1 0.10 to 0.06; dead source replaced.
C-02.base_name: GLP-1 Drugs Reshape Consumer Spending Patterns

C-03.rationale: Confirmed by Henkel's own price/volume pattern and by L'Oréal and Kérastase growth. Kept as the hair premiumisation anchor; T-14 becomes its ingredient reason-to-believe.
C-03.corrections: 'L'Oréal Professional Products +15% in 2025' wrong (+7.5% LFL; +15% was premium haircare only); '2-3x mass' overstated (about 1.5x in value); Olaplex added; GP1 0.20 to 0.18 because the mass unit decline is now its own line (C-35).

C-04.rationale: Clinical-efficacy premiumisation is the umbrella for the science-led hair stories and is visible in Circana and NIQ prestige data. Kept.
C-04.corrections: Green Claims Directive reference replaced by EmpCo (Directive 2024/825, 27 Sep 2026); unverified '3,000 formulations' claim removed; GP1 0.08 to 0.10.

C-05.rationale: Ageing is one of two true Megatrends in the set; only the evidenced HCB mechanisms (grey-coverage colour, gentle and scalp care) are kept. Absorbs the LHC ageing slice of C-30 through category exposure instead of a clone trend.
C-05.corrections: Packaging-ergonomics story removed (not a pool driver); probability 5 to 4; GP1 0.12 to 0.08; dead Eurostat link replaced.
C-05.base_name: Silver Economy — Aging Population Shifts Category Demand

C-06.rationale: The base described 2025 disinflation and ECB cuts; the 2026 reality is energy-shock inflation, an ECB hike and entrenched value-seeking. Kept and rewritten; the goods-to-services wallet shift, shrinkflation laws and the French promo cap are folded in as description content.
C-06.corrections: ECB-cuts and 'stabilising' sentences deleted; H1 2026 price/volume pattern inserted; probability 4 to 5; peak 2029 to 2028; North America exposure raised to 4.
C-06.base_name: Cost-of-Living Squeeze and Persistent Trading Down

C-07.rationale: Scalp care as a regimen step is confirmed in US prestige data and by Dove and L'Oréal launches. Kept; T-04 (microbiome) was the same GP1 counted twice and is folded in.
C-07.corrections: 'USD 88.2bn to 150.5bn' was the global hair-care total, not scalp care (deleted); stale 'Henkel has no scalp line' corrected; GP1 0.08 to 0.06.
C-07.base_name: Scalp Care Emerges as Standalone Category

C-08.rationale: Men's grooming is a real personal-care mesotrend but HCB's exposure is thin (Men Perfect, Taft/got2b) and the sizing was report-mill grade. Its thinning and grey-blending slice is carried in C-10.
C-08.corrections: Statista/Allied sizing (USD 23.6bn, 7.65% CAGR) not found on the cited page; Vernel fragrance idea removed.

C-09.rationale: Same mechanism as C-28 (scent-led premiumisation of laundry additives), a straight double count.
C-09.corrections: 'Scent boosters +15% in Southern Europe' unsourced; replaced by the Unilever-cited global series in C-28.
C-09.base_name: Fragrance and Sensory Premiumization in Home Care

C-10.rationale: The single thinning-demand driver: GLP-1 shedding, tele-derm Rx, supplements and cosmetic thickening. Absorbs C-32, the hair side of C-23 and the men's slice of C-08.
C-10.corrections: Fortune Business Insights sizing (grade D) replaced by JAAD cohort evidence and the Nutrafol GLP-1 pivot; AAD 404 removed; GP1 0.06 to 0.05; GLP-1 shedding counted once (C-02).
C-10.base_name: Hair Loss and Thinning Treatments Enter Consumer Mainstream

C-11.rationale: Dupe culture is now a cross-cohort value-equivalence norm (Circana 2026), not a Gen Z story. Kept and reframed; the LHC paragraph is owned by C-01.
C-11.corrections: Unverified minimalist-routine claim removed; Olaplex exposure added; GP1 0.12 to 0.08; probability 5 to 4; peak 2030 to 2029.
C-11.base_name: Gen Z Dupe Culture and Ingredient Literacy

C-13.rationale: PPWR sets no refill or re-use target for detergents or household chemicals; retailer refill stations remain sub-1% uptake. Not a pool driver; the brand-side refill pouch is a format inside T-03.
C-13.corrections: 'PPWR refill targets confirmed for 2030' wrong (Regulation 2025/40 targets cover take-away food and beverage, transport and white-goods packaging).
C-13.base_name: Refill and Reuse Economy in Household Care

C-14.rationale: Refresh between washes is one occasion inside a single garment-care trend; merged into C-29.
C-14.corrections: Febreze is an air-care brand reported in P&G Home Care and passed USD 1bn in fiscal 2011; it was not built on fabric refresh. 'Fastest-growing LHC occasion' unsupported.
C-14.base_name: Between-Wash Fabric Care as Standalone Consumption Occasion

C-15.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, key HCB claim stale
C-15.rationale: A real occasion (dry shampoo, styling refreshers) but a format-level Microtrend with immaterial influence (+0.04 pp); styling premium is inside C-03. Kept on the NEXT list with the Batiste and NYM Clean Freak facts.
C-15.corrections: 'Batiste 40%+ share' unverified; 'got2b under-invests versus Batiste' is stale (HCB now owns NYM Clean Freak).
C-15.base_name: Hair Styling and Maintenance Between Washes

C-16.rationale: Domestic-brand capture in China is real (57.4% domestic share in 2025, fifth year of gains) and largely realised. Kept at a lower weight.
C-16.corrections: Share figure re-attributed to CAFFCI (not Euromonitor); 'nationalism' framing dropped; HCB exposure corrected post Vidal Sassoon; GP1 0.12 to 0.07; start 2023 to 2021; probability 5 to 4.
C-16.base_name: China C-Beauty Nationalism and Domestic Brand Preference

C-17.rationale: India is a real growth market but HCB's exposure is near zero, and the line duplicated X-06's mechanism. Carried as the India sub-exposure (about 0.03 GP1) inside the consolidated growth-market driver.
C-17.corrections: 'USD 30bn' not Redseer's figure (USD 23bn FY25 to USD 40bn by 2030); '14% washing-machine penetration' stale (about 20%).
C-17.base_name: India Premium Affordability and Middle-Class Expansion

C-18.rationale: The Hispanic demographic dividend is real for the horizon but delayed by the 2025-27 enforcement and migration shock; kept with a later onset and lower weight. The near-term shock itself is carried by C-34 and G-15.
C-18.corrections: Hispanic growth halved in 2025 (+1.35m vs +2.29m); 'no curl-care line' stale (NYM Curl Talk); start 2024 to 2027, peak 2031 to 2033, GP1 0.14 to 0.08, probability 5 to 4.
C-18.base_name: US Hispanic/Latino Consumers Drive Hair and LHC Category Growth

C-19.rationale: Southeast Asia is a real digital-first market but the line repeated the growth-market mechanism and its channel content belongs to K-04. Carried as the SEA sub-exposure (about 0.02 GP1).
C-19.corrections: 'World's highest e-commerce growth' not established; K-beauty framing replaced by Chinese and local digital-native brands; Indonesia halal (17 Oct 2026) noted as a dated regulation.

C-20.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED on Brazil, CONTRADICTED on nearshoring
C-20.rationale: Mexico-anchored LatAm growth is real; the nearshoring bonus is not in the trade data and Brazil reaches HCB only through professional hair. Carried as the LatAm sub-exposure (about 0.05 GP1).
C-20.corrections: Brazil is number three globally (not four); '+40% manufacturing investment' unsupported; Brazil premium-hair content moved to K-07.

C-21.rationale: A claims-language shift, not a demand mechanism; double counts C-05, C-07, C-10 and C-03. Three of four sources unverifiable.
C-21.corrections: 'USD 120bn anti-ageing by 2030' untraceable; '70% of disposable income held by 60+' not in the AARP source.
C-21.base_name: Longevity Medicine Crossover into Beauty and Hair Care

C-22.rationale: Sheets test poorly (Consumer Reports, Mar 2026) and the 2026 format event is P&G's premium fibre tile, not value sheets. The dry-format shift belongs inside T-03.
C-22.corrections: 'Sheets reach 5% of a major market' trigger replaced by a dry-format share trigger on HCB's own panel data.

C-23.rationale: The cited Lancet paper does not exist; no HCB pool mechanism; double counts C-10, C-02 and C-09. The one useful fact (Nutrafol as GLP-1 complement) moves to C-10.
C-23.corrections: 'The Lancet: Clinical Efficacy in Hybrid Beauty (2025)' is not a real article; Harvard Chan and Circana links are homepages.

C-24.rationale: Textured hair as a mainstream category is real, North America first. Kept with corrected sourcing and re-weighted regional exposure.
C-24.corrections: '65% of the world has textured hair' is a 2018 US survey statistic; 'USD 8bn+, 7-9% CAGR' unverified; 'Henkel has no credible offering' stale (NYM Curl Talk); GP1 0.08 to 0.06.
C-24.base_name: Natural/Textured Hair as Mainstream Global Category

C-25.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED on fertility, CONTRADICTED on households
C-25.rationale: Sub-replacement fertility is a Megatrend, but household counts still rise to 2035, so the volume effect is later and smaller than the base assumed. Kept volume-only so it does not double count C-05.
C-25.corrections: 'Fewer households forming' deleted (contradicted by Eurostat/Destatis); figures updated (EU TFR 1.34, Korea 0.80 rising); GP1 0.12 to 0.06; start 2024 to 2028, back-loaded.
C-25.base_name: Birth Rate Collapse and Household Atomisation

C-26.rationale: Tween skincare is a discrete phenomenon with sub-threshold evidence in HCB's categories; no reshaping of the competitive set.
C-26.corrections: Category evidence fragmentary; downgrade to Signal.

C-27.rationale: The logic holds (dishwasher penetration catch-up drives ADW), the numbers did not. Re-based to HCB's real ADW geography (Southern and Eastern Europe, Türkiye, MEA).
C-27.corrections: China penetration about 3% (not 12%); Germany 77.3% (not 71%); US 72.7% (not 68%); India/Brazil/Mexico figures unsupported; GP1 0.06 to 0.04; peak 2034 linear.
C-27.base_name: Hand-Dish to Auto-Dish Conversion in Emerging Markets

C-28.rationale: Scent-led premiumisation of laundry additives is a real, growing pool that P&G leads. Kept as the single additive driver, absorbing C-09.
C-28.corrections: 'EU EUR 2bn, EUR 4.5bn by 2030, US USD 1.8bn' contradicted by the only public series (EUR 1.9bn global 2023, EUR 3bn by 2028); Vernel Aroma Boost / Silan Powerboosters sentences removed; start 2025 to 2023.
C-28.base_name: Laundry Scent Boosters as Structural Premium Category

C-29.rationale: Made the single fabric-care occasion driver (specialty care, fibre renewal, refresh, longevity norms), absorbing C-14, E-08 and G-12, which told one consumer story from three angles. Henkel's own reporting now confirms the commercial thesis.
C-29.corrections: 'Technical fabrics 35% of wardrobe' not found in WGSN or Textile Exchange (polyester 59% of fibre output is the verifiable fact); probability 3 to 4; GP1 0.05 to 0.08; start 2026 to 2024.
C-29.base_name: Delicates & Performance Fabric Care Revival (Perwoll Occasion)

C-30.rationale: A clone of the ageing Megatrend with no verifiable numbers; the LHC ageing exposure is set through C-05's category scores instead.
C-30.corrections: '60+ = 40% of European LHC spend', '1.8x home hygiene', 'pet ownership +38%' found in no source; Euromonitor URL dead; OECD and AARP links are homepages.
C-30.base_name: Longevity Economy — LHC / Home Hygiene Split

C-31.rationale: A single unverifiable statistic about Gen Z cleaning literacy; no mechanism that moves the pool.
C-31.corrections: Core statistic untraceable; contradicted in spirit by available evidence.
C-31.base_name: Cleaning-Fluency Generational Decline (Gen Z Home-Care Literacy)

C-32.rationale: Tele-derm hair Rx is a channel caveat on thinning demand, not a driver: Hims & Hers' entire FY2025 revenue was USD 2.35bn across all specialties. One sentence goes to C-10.

C-33.rationale: The Shein/Temu price-floor thesis was overtaken by the EU customs reform (EUR 150 exemption abolished, EUR 3 duty) and platform localisation; a watch sentence lives in X-16.
C-33.corrections: Sources unverifiable; 2026 EU customs facts added to X-16 and G-08.
C-33.base_name: Ultra-Fast-Fashion Beauty: Shein/Temu-Style Price Floor Collapse

C-34.rationale: Gap: the base had no North American volume headwind from the 2025-27 immigration reversal, which slows household formation and hits the Hispanic hair and laundry base.
C-34.corrections: New driver, Contraction, probability 4, GP1 0.08, 2025-2029 front-loaded.

C-35.rationale: Gap: the base modelled hair premiumisation only as an upside; the mass unit decline that funds it is the Contraction counterpart.
C-35.corrections: New driver, Contraction, probability 4, GP1 0.10, 2025-2031 linear.

C-36.rationale: Gap: the base had no currency driver while its two largest Expansion lines were stated in organic terms; Türkiye and Egypt hyperinflation and IMEA/LatAm depreciation dilute euro gross profit.
C-36.corrections: New driver, Contraction, probability 5, GP1 0.12, 2025-2030 linear. Convention decision required (euro-reported vs constant-currency pool).

X-06.rationale: The anchor of the consolidated growth-market driver: IMEA double-digit organic growth confirmed through H1 2026. Six regional Expansion lines modelled one mechanism six times; now one driver with sub-region weights in the regional exposure scores. Force reassigned from Competitive to Consumer.
X-06.corrections: Stated in organic terms with the FX dilution moved to C-36; probability 5 to 4; GP1 0.14 to 0.15 for the merged driver.
X-06.base_name: Emerging Markets Growth Divergence — IMEA Leads

X-09.rationale: Sub-Saharan Africa's demographics are real but the 'USD 200bn by 2030' figure and 'Lions on the Move III' citation do not exist. Carried as the SSA sub-exposure (about 0.03 GP1, back-loaded).
X-09.corrections: 'USD 200bn FMCG by 2030' untraceable; 'Lions on the Move III' does not exist.

X-14.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED on legal facts, CONTRADICTED on relevance
X-14.rationale: AfCFTA is a real instrument but there is no measurable intra-African preferential trade in HCB's categories yet; kept as a dated watch note inside X-06.
X-14.corrections: 'Operational tariff harmonisation 2026-28' overstated; Category B phase-down began 1 Jan 2026 for some members only.
X-14.base_name: AfCFTA Implementation Unlocks Pan-African Competitive Pressure

K-01.rationale: Discount is still the largest and, outside Germany, the fastest-growing physical channel; the pool mechanism is trade-margin dilution and price-ladder compression. Kept; variety discounters folded in.
K-01.corrections: German plateau and US expansion added; management-response text removed; GP1 0.20 to 0.15; curve linear to s_curve; peak 2031 to 2029.
K-01.base_name: Discount Retail Channel Expansion in Europe

K-02.rationale: E-commerce and marketplace share gain at lower brand net margin is a 10-15 year reshaping across categories and regions; tier raised to Macrotrend. Absorbs K-06.
K-02.corrections: 'Stabilisation at 12-15%' unsourced and above German FMCG online share; Persil/Somat S&S instruction removed; GP1 0.08 to 0.10.

K-03.rationale: Buyer-power concentration is re-forming through alliances (Concordis, Eurelec, Everest) and M&A; kept with verified facts and the EU territorial-supply-constraint watch item.
K-03.corrections: DBA strategy text and unsourced '40-50% of European HCB revenue' removed; probability 5 to 4; peak 2031 to 2030.

K-04.rationale: TikTok Shop is a scaled beauty channel (US GMV USD 15.1bn in 2025; beauty the largest category) but not a top-5 FMCG channel and irrelevant for LHC. Kept, hair only; K-10 folded in.
K-04.corrections: 'Top-5 FMCG channel', Sally Beauty and '4.7% conversion' claims removed; GP1 0.10 to 0.06; probability 5 to 4.
K-04.base_name: TikTok Shop Becomes Top-5 FMCG Channel

K-06.rationale: Subscription and auto-replenishment lock-in is a sub-mechanism of e-commerce economics, not a separate driver.
K-06.corrections: Rewe left Payback (Dec 2024) and Edeka joined (Jan 2025): named examples were reversed; no public S&S metric exists.
K-06.base_name: FMCG Subscription and Loyalty Ecosystem Lock-in

K-07.rationale: Professional and bond-repair brands crossing into retail lift the hair price ladder; confirmed by L'Oréal and Henkel reporting. Kept.
K-07.corrections: '+15% in 2025' wrong (+7.5% LFL FY2025, +12.6% H1 2026); FMI source deleted; Kérastase-playbook strategy text removed; start 2025 to 2023.
K-07.base_name: Professional Salon Channel to Consumer Crossover

K-08.rationale: Identical eMarketer series to T-06; merged so the retail-media tax is counted once.
K-08.corrections: '8-12% of brand net revenue' unsourced and dropped.
K-08.base_name: US Retail Media Networks Reshape Brand-Customer Economics

K-09.rationale: The 'retail power dissolves' premise is the opposite of what happened: OpenAI's Instant Checkout was retired in March 2026 because retailers kept checkout and data. Carried as one sub-mechanism (retailer-owned agents) inside T-11.
K-09.base_name: Agentic Commerce Reshapes Retailer-Brand Power Dynamics

K-10.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, exaggerated for the West
K-10.rationale: Live commerce is a minority format in Western TikTok Shop (Momentum Works puts US Live at about 8% of attributed GMV in H1 2026); a format within K-04, not a driver.
K-10.corrections: Take-rate and margin caveat carried into K-04.

K-11.rationale: Loyalty data is monetised through the same retail media networks (84.51, Tesco, Payback); same money as T-06.
K-11.corrections: Loyalty-scheme facts (Edeka to Payback 2025, Rewe Bonus, Lidl Plus) carried into T-06.
K-11.base_name: Retailer Loyalty Program Cannibalisation of Trade Spend

K-12.rationale: Gap: the largest HCB-relevant channel driver missing from the base; dm, Rossmann and Müller keep gaining share in Germany and continental Europe with deep own-label ranges in hair, body and household care.
K-12.corrections: New driver, Contraction, probability 4, GP1 0.10, 2023-2030 s_curve.

X-01.rationale: A dated transaction (Signal), not a trend; replaced by the pattern-level driver X-17 (incumbent retrenchment across Vestacy, P&G exits, Beiersdorf, Coty).
X-01.corrections: Deal was 'up to USD 4.8bn' enterprise value with Reckitt retaining 30% and about USD 2.2bn net proceeds, not a USD 4.8bn cash sale; management actions removed.

X-02.fc: CONFIRMED on numbers, STALE on framing
X-02.rationale: Unilever's beauty-first investment (Dove fibre repair and scalp, K18, 16.1% A&P) is evidence for the scale-leader pattern X-15, not a driver on its own.

X-03.fc: CONFIRMED on FY2025, STALE on current
X-03.rationale: P&G's superiority and unit-dose pressure is the laundry leg of X-15.
X-03.corrections: 'Ariel The Big One 40% of UK growth' is P&G's own claim; FY2026 organic +1% with Fabric & Home Care flat added.
X-03.base_name: P&G Superiority Framework and Innovation Fortress

X-04.rationale: The channel facts are real and stronger than stated; 'indie' framing too narrow. Becomes the anchor evidence of X-16 (social-native and Asian challengers).
X-04.corrections: '3-4x YoY (Marketplace Pulse, Jungle Scout)' unverified, both URLs 404; replaced by Momentum Works GMV data.
X-04.base_name: Indie Brand Omnichannel Pivot via TikTok Shop

X-05.rationale: The 'tariff-free EU via Temu and TikTok Shop' thesis was overtaken by the EU customs reform; Chinese brand share in Europe remains under 2%. Watch trigger inside X-16.
X-05.corrections: Technavio source removed; EU customs facts (EUR 150 exemption abolished, EUR 3 duty) passed to G-08.
X-05.base_name: Chinese FMCG Brands Enter European Market

X-07.rationale: L'Oréal's R&I, beauty-tech and professional omnichannel scale is the hair anchor of X-15.
X-07.corrections: R&I EUR 1.38bn (3.1%), not EUR 1.7bn (4%); Professional Products +7.5% FY2025; K-SCAN +23% is company-stated.

X-08.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED on the wave, CONTRADICTED on hair specificity
X-08.rationale: Korean cosmetics exports hit a record USD 11.4bn in 2025, but the wave is skincare-led; the hair extension is the explicit uncertainty inside X-16.
X-08.corrections: Amorepacific share and most base numbers unverifiable; MFDS export data substituted.
X-08.base_name: K-Beauty and J-Beauty Export Wave into NA and EU Hair Care

X-10.rationale: Amazon cut its private label to under 20 brands in 2023 (about 1% of retail sales) and its 2025 moves are food-only; marketplace fees, retail media and agents are already in K-02, T-06 and T-11.
X-10.corrections: 'US PL +4.4% vs +1.1%' is a PLMA/Circana all-outlet figure, not Amazon; Morgan Stanley URL 404.

X-11.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, wrong date and scope
X-11.rationale: A single dated partnership (announced 17 Mar 2026 at NVIDIA GTC, not CES) and a sub-signal of X-07; one sentence of evidence in X-15.
X-11.corrections: Date, venue and scope corrected; repeats X-07's R&I error.
X-11.base_name: L'Oreal NVIDIA AI Molecule Discovery Partnership

X-12.fc: CONFIRMED deal list, CONTRADICTED on Henkel, double count
X-12.rationale: A list of transactions by named actors with no mechanism of its own; the verified deals become evidence in X-15 and X-16, Wella and Coty move to X-18.
X-12.corrections: Henkel statement corrected; e.l.f./Rhode, L'Oréal/Medik8 and Color Wow, Unilever/Dr. Squatch verified.
X-12.base_name: DTC/Indie Brand Acquisition Arms Race Intensifies

X-13.rationale: Retailer vertical integration into HCB categories is not happening: Walmart's plants are milk and beef, Schwarz Produktion is food and paper, Kirkland is supplier-sourced. The premium own-label tier is a C-01 mechanism; Henkel itself exited NA private-label laundry in April 2025.
X-13.corrections: 'Aldi expanding Lacura into laundry pods' wrong (Lacura is skin care; Tandil/Almat are the laundry labels); Investor Day source is a generic results page.
X-13.base_name: Walmart / Costco / Aldi Vertical Integration into FMCG Supply

X-15.rationale: Replaces four named-actor Signals (X-02, X-03, X-07, X-11) with one pattern-level driver: scale-leader innovation and A&P escalation in hair and laundry.
X-15.corrections: Contraction, probability 5, GP1 0.25, 2024-2032 linear; calibrated to reproduce the four Signals' combined 2035 contribution of about -0.9 to -1.0 pp.

X-16.rationale: Replaces X-04, X-08, X-05, X-12 and the residue of C-33 with one driver: social-commerce-native and Asian challenger brands fragmenting hair-care share.

X-17.rationale: Replaces X-01 with a pattern across five actors: incumbent retrenchment and portfolio pruning open share windows in home care and body care.
X-17.corrections: Expansion, probability 3, GP1 0.08, 2025-2028 front-loaded; ADW exposure 0.

X-18.rationale: Gap: the contraction side of the professional hair channel (salon volume erosion, pro-brand migration to retail, L'Oréal PPD dominance, Wella re-listing, diversion), material now that M&A has doubled Henkel's professional exposure.

T-01.rationale: AI and automation productivity is one Macrotrend, not three; T-05, T-10 and the salon-diagnostics point of T-07 merge here. The pool effect is net of competitive reinvestment since private label and challengers get the same tools.
T-01.corrections: L'Oréal R&I EUR 1.38bn (3.1%), not EUR 1.7bn (4%); '725 patents' and 'Deloitte 67%' unverified; combined GP1 0.24 to 0.08; probability 5 to 4.

T-02.rationale: Enzymes are commercial and growing (Novonesis), biosurfactants niche, fermentation and synthetic biology the long tail; one substitution driver, absorbing T-15 and T-16. Tier lowered to Mesotrend.
T-02.corrections: Wrong PFAS/microplastics linkage removed; probability 4 to 3; GP1 0.10 to 0.05; start 2027, peak 2033.

T-03.rationale: Compaction and dry formats reshape the laundry and ADW format mix, logistics and price architecture (P&G Tide evo tiles national from April 2026); tier raised to Mesotrend. Absorbs C-22, the brand-refill element of C-13 and the format mechanism of E-02 and E-10.
T-03.corrections: 'Persil Discs success' unsupported; shampoo bars moved to hair; GP1 0.07 to 0.10.

T-04.rationale: Same Circana scalp figure as C-07; an ingredient and claims layer, not a driver.
T-04.corrections: Grand View and Verified Market Research sources deleted; 'P&G front-of-pack branding' unverified.
T-04.base_name: Microbiome Science for Hair and Skin

T-05.rationale: Manufacturing automation is the plant-operations leg of the merged AI and automation driver.
T-05.corrections: Deloitte 2026 outlook and Unilever digital-twin figures carried as evidence.

T-06.rationale: The single largest verified channel-economics driver: retail media and retailer data monetisation as a visibility tax (US USD 60bn in 2025, Europe growing four times faster than digital). Absorbs K-08 and K-11; force reassigned to Customer.
T-06.corrections: 'Primary FMCG channel' title is a category error (a cost line, not a channel); '8-12% of net revenue' unsourced; Mordor/Adtelligent sources replaced; GP1 0.18 against a triple-counted 0.40; start 2024 to 2022.
T-06.base_name: Retail Media Networks as Primary FMCG Channel

T-07.rationale: One company's tool with company-stated uplift (K-SCAN +23%); the salon-diagnostics point sits in T-01, shade matching in C-05.
T-07.corrections: Gartner and CB Insights URLs dead; Similarweb and L'Oréal links homepages.

T-08.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED on existence, CONTRADICTED on scale
T-08.rationale: Rebuilt: OEM auto-dosing and platform-mediated replenishment shift volume, format and channel control, a mild Contraction for a brand owner. Persil Smartwash was a management response with minimal adoption and moves to the Signal watch list.
T-08.corrections: Direction Expansion to Contraction; probability 4 to 3; GP1 0.07 to 0.05; report-mill sources removed.
T-08.base_name: Connected Appliances and Auto-Dosing Transform Detergent Economics

T-10.rationale: Generative-AI marketing efficiency is the marketing leg of the merged AI driver.
T-10.corrections: '40-60% content cost reduction confirmed by P&G and Unilever' has no source; only McKinsey's 5-15% of marketing spend estimate is A-grade.
T-10.base_name: Generative AI Content and Marketing Efficiency Revolution

T-11.rationale: Agentic commerce intermediating low-consideration replenishment is a real Macrotrend, but one driver, not three: T-12 and K-09 merge here (combined GP1 0.44 to 0.15). Rewritten to the September 2026 state (Alexa for Shopping, Google UCP, OpenAI retreat, Visa/Mastercard protocols).
T-11.corrections: 'Alexa+ Feb 2026' wrong (Feb 2025); Kearney 60% and Gartner 25% (a B2B statistic) removed; probability 5 to 4; peak 2031 to 2032.
T-11.base_name: Agentic Commerce: AI Agents Make Autonomous Purchase Decisions

T-12.rationale: Brand invisibility in agent ranking is a paragraph of T-11, not a separate driver.
T-12.corrections: '58% of retailers (Deloitte)' unverified; BCG URL 404; Smartwash defence is a management response.
T-12.base_name: AI Agent Brand Invisibility in Low-Consideration Categories

T-13.corrections: '35% vs 13.6%', '4,700%' and CTR figures deleted; all four sources replaced; probability 5 to 4; GP1 0.12 to 0.08; start 2025 to 2024.
T-13.base_name: Generative Search (GEO) Replaces Traditional Product Discovery — Expanded

T-14.rationale: Peptides and bond-builders are the reason-to-believe layer of hair premiumisation; efficacy evidence at cosmetic concentrations is thin.
T-14.corrections: 'USD 2-3bn peptide hair market' cites the peptide therapeutics (pharma) market; Grand View source deleted.

T-15.base_name: Precision Fermentation Disrupts FMCG Ingredient Supply Chains

T-16.rationale: Zymergen was liquidated in 2024 and Ginkgo is restructuring; palm-free surfactants exist at niche scale only. One sentence on novel molecules in T-02.
T-16.base_name: Synthetic Biology Enables Novel Surfactants and Fragrances

T-17.rationale: PubMed indexes ten neurocosmetics papers in total, none an RCT; no product pool, no HCB mechanism.

T-18.rationale: Connected dispensers and smart mirrors: three of four sources dead, no adoption evidence; the replenishment angle is inside T-08.
T-18.corrections: Samsung, IDC and Miele URLs dead or irrelevant.
T-18.base_name: Bathroom and Laundry-Room IoT — Connected Dispensers, Smart Mirrors

T-19.rationale: All four sources fail (Mintel homepage, Givaudan and IFF 404, HBR article does not exist); no measurable pool.
T-19.base_name: Neuro-Scents: Functional Fragrance with Measured Neuro-Benefit

G-01.rationale: PFAS in cosmetics is one component of the EU ingredient-restriction stack (PFHxA Oct 2026, universal restriction 2029+) and of the US state bans; not a standalone line.
G-01.corrections: '1 January 2026 EU cosmetics PFAS ban' was the French law, not EU; LHC coatings sentence deleted.

G-02.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, central risk claim CONTRADICTED
G-02.rationale: Real dated instrument (Regulation 2023/2055) with clear gates; kept with the PVA sentences removed because water-soluble pod film is not in scope.
G-02.corrections: Detergents deadline corrected from 2029 to Oct 2028; PVA/pod risk deleted; GP1 0.10 to 0.05.

G-03.rationale: The EU cosmetics ingredient-restriction stack (Omnibus VII/VIII, 56 allergens 2026/28, PFHxA, D4/D5/D6) is the live cosmetics compliance driver; kept, absorbing the EU part of G-01.
G-03.corrections: Detergents Regulation sentence moved to G-16; allergen and PFHxA gates added; GP1 0.15 to 0.12; timing 2025-2028 linear.
G-03.base_name: EU Cosmetics Regulation Omnibus VII/VIII Revision

G-04.rationale: Packaging regulation and EPR fees are one cost stack (PPWR 2026/2028/2030/2038 plus EU, UK and US state eco-modulation); G-04, E-04 and the label part of G-07 triple-counted it. Merged with geography extended to the UK and US.
G-04.corrections: Dates corrected; '3-5x trigger-spray malus' unsourced and deleted; GP1 0.07 (G-04) and 0.04 (E-04) become 0.15 for the merged stack (top of the regulatory calibration band); curve step to linear.
G-04.base_name: EU PPWR — Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation

G-05.rationale: EmpCo (Directive 2024/825) applies from 27 September 2026 and is live; the Green Claims Directive is stalled and demoted to context.
G-05.corrections: CMA URL 404 and EcoAct vendor source replaced; GP1 0.08 to 0.04.
G-05.base_name: EU Green Claims Directive / EmpCo Enforcement

G-06.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, mechanics wrong for HCB
G-06.rationale: EUDR (30 Dec 2026) and CSDDD (26 Jul 2029, post-Omnibus) form one nature and due-diligence stack; HCB is a downstream user with pass-through cost. Absorbs G-11.
G-06.corrections: HCB compliance mechanics corrected; start 2026 to 2027; GP1 0.05 to 0.04.

G-07.rationale: The Digital Product Passport that binds HCB comes through the Detergents Regulation (23 Sep 2029), not a generic 'QR codes from 2027'; the label element is packaging-stack cost.
G-07.corrections: 'QR codes from 2027' wrong; ESPR working plan does not cover detergents or cosmetics.

G-08.rationale: One US tariff regime, not two: G-08 and G-09 merge, rewritten to the post-IEEPA regime (Supreme Court struck IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026; Section 301/232/122 remain).
G-08.corrections: 'Section 301 25-60% now effective' conflated three regimes; combined GP1 0.22 to 0.06; probability 5 to 4; peak 2029 to 2027.

G-09.rationale: 'USTR Feb 2026 notice confirms escalation' was wrong: February 2026 was the Supreme Court striking down IEEPA tariffs; refunds offset 2026 for Church & Dwight and P&G. Merged into G-08.
G-09.corrections: Aerosol-can metals channel and refund evidence carried into G-08.
G-09.base_name: US Tariffs and Reshoring Pressure on Imported FMCG Inputs

G-10.rationale: The AI Act does not classify FMCG formulation, marketing or forecasting tools as high-risk; the Digital Omnibus delayed the high-risk provisions further. Fails the relevance test.
G-10.corrections: Dates stale after the Digital Omnibus; applicability wrong.
G-10.base_name: EU AI Act Compliance Costs and Speed-to-Market Friction

G-11.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED as frameworks, CONTRADICTED as mandate
G-11.rationale: GBF and TNFD are frameworks without a corporate compliance timetable; the one dated instrument (CSDDD 2029) is the nature component of G-06.
G-11.base_name: Biodiversity Regulation and Nature-Related Supply Chain Mandates

G-12.fc: STALE on instruments, CONTRADICTED on relevance
G-12.rationale: The EU textile strategy's binding instruments regulate apparel, not HCB; the residual consumer-awareness effect sits inside C-29.
G-12.corrections: ESPR destruction ban (19 Jul 2026), DPP registry (20 Jul 2026), textile EPR Directive 2025/1892 dated but not HCB-binding.
G-12.base_name: EU Textile Strategy and Circular Fashion Mandates

G-13.fc: PARTLY CONFIRMED, several state claims wrong
G-13.rationale: MoCRA is in force (GMP and allergen rules delayed) and US state ingredient bans are dated (WA/CO/MN/CA 2025, VT/ME 2026, OR/NM 2027); kept, absorbing the US part of G-01, with the federal deregulatory turn noted.
G-13.corrections: NY and Prop 65 statements corrected; Washington phenylenediamine and formaldehyde-releaser bans added; probability 5 to 4; GP1 0.08 to 0.06.
G-13.base_name: MoCRA + US State Cosmetics Regulation (CA Prop 65, NY, WA)

G-14.rationale: The NGO coalition, Bloomberg piece, JRC report and '15-25 bps' estimate could not be found; the real instrument is the Detergents and Surfactants Regulation 2026/405 with its film biodegradability criteria (delegated act by Mar 2029, compliance by Mar 2032).
G-14.corrections: Evidence base replaced entirely by the EUR-Lex text; probability 3 to 4; GP1 0.18 to 0.12.
G-14.base_name: Biodegradability Standards Tighten Around PVA Unit-Dose Films

G-15.rationale: Gap: SNAP work requirements from November 2025 and state cost-share from FY2028 are a dated federal instrument already measurable in US mass-market units.

G-16.rationale: EU Detergents and Surfactants Regulation 2026/405 (DPP and digital label from 23 Sep 2029, film biodegradability criteria by 2032, phosphorus review) plus CLP relabelling 2026-29; substitutes G-14 and absorbs the DPP part of G-07.

G-17.rationale: Gap: the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (2024/3019) makes cosmetics producers fund at least 80% of quaternary treatment through extended producer responsibility (schemes by end-2028, fees from 2029); absent from the base entirely.

E-01.rationale: B50 is live (blending 50% from 1 July 2026) and the squeeze runs through palm kernel and coconut oil, the oils HCB actually buys, not crude palm oil. Kept and re-titled; tier lowered to Mesotrend.
E-01.corrections: B50 status updated from 'doubts' to live; substitution moved out (management response); probability 4 to 5; timing 2024-2027 front-loaded.
E-01.base_name: Palm Oil Supply Chain Disruption (Indonesia B50)

E-02.rationale: Water stress is a Megatrend context; the only pool mechanism is the format shift toward concentrated and low-water products, which T-03 already carries.
E-02.corrections: WRI Aqueduct facts are from Aug 2023 (still current release); the three 'opportunities' were management responses.

E-03.rationale: EU carbon-cost pass-through (ETS EUR 80-90/t, ETS2 from 2028, CBAM definitive 2026, downstream metal goods 2028) is one driver; E-11 merges in. Scope 3 reporting is not a pool driver.
E-03.corrections: Surfactant-inclusion claim deleted; combined GP1 0.09 to 0.10; curve step to linear 2026-2030.
E-03.base_name: Carbon Border Adjustment and Scope 3 Reporting

E-04.rationale: EPR fee escalation is the same packaging cost stack as PPWR; merged with geography extended to the UK and US.

E-05.rationale: Aedes albopictus expansion is real (ECDC) but disease seasons are volatile and Insect Control is one niche category; influence +0.02 pp. Watch list with the ECDC map as refresh source.

E-06.rationale: Kearney's 2026 index shows US manufacturing imports at a four-year high, so the reshoring thesis is not in the data; the real upstream driver is European chemical supply-base erosion (Cefic closures), now inside E-07.
E-06.corrections: 'Chinese surfactant suppliers about 30% of European supply' and '2-5%' figures unsourced.
E-06.base_name: Supply Chain Nearshoring and Geopolitical Diversification

E-07.fc: CONFIRMED in direction, corrected in detail
E-07.rationale: Structural European energy disadvantage (electricity about 2x, gas 3-6x US) plus the 2026 gas shock; kept, Europe only, tier lowered to Mesotrend. Absorbs the E-06 substitute and demotes E-09 to a watch item.
E-07.corrections: '2-3x' replaced by IEA/Eurostat figures; nuclear phase-out sentence deleted; probability 4 to 5; GP1 0.07 to 0.06; start 2024 to 2022.
E-07.base_name: Energy Cost Volatility and European Manufacturing Competitiveness

E-08.rationale: Textile longevity as a consumer norm is one angle of the garment-care occasion driver C-29.

E-08.base_name: Textile Longevity and Garment Life Extension Economy

E-09.rationale: Munich Re reports Europe 'got off rather lightly' in 2025 (USD 11bn losses vs a USD 35bn ten-year average); '15-20% annual insurance increases' unsourced. Physical risk belongs in the risk register, not the pool model.
E-09.corrections: Both headline claims wrong or unsourced.
E-09.base_name: Climate Adaptation Costs for European Manufacturing

E-10.rationale: No regulator in the EU, US, India, China or the GCC has proposed water-content limits on consumer products; the format architecture point sits in T-03.
E-10.corrections: Regulation does not exist; statistics stale.
E-10.base_name: Freshwater Crisis Accelerates Waterless Formulation Mandate

E-11.rationale: Scope 3 mandates do not price surfactants; the same ETS/CBAM driver as E-03.
E-11.corrections: Surfactant-inclusion claim and 2030 step rationale deleted.
